studies.Study: Wang Y et al. (2021) [PMID: 32238007] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Dietary Intakes of Trace Elements and the Risk of Kidney Cancer: The Singapore Chinese Health Study.
studies.Title: Dietary Intakes of Trace Elements and the Risk of Kidney Cancer: The Singapore Chinese Health Study.
studies.Authors: Wang Y, Jafar TH, Jin A, Yuan JM, Koh WP
studies.comparison_type: Highest vs lowest quartile of dietary zinc intake

sample_size.excerpt: Background: Epidemiological studies have demonstrated separately that patients with kidney stone may have higher dietary intake of zinc and higher risk of developing kidney cancer. We prospectively assessed the associations of dietary zinc and other trace elements with kidney cancer risk for the first time.Methods: We used data from the prospective Singapore Chinese Health Study that recruited 63,257 adult Chinese residing in Singapore between 1993 and 1998.

cases.excerpt: We identified incident cancer cases via linkage with nationwide cancer registry, and used Cox proportional hazard models to compute hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) for the association with kidney cancer risk.Results: There were 229 incident kidney cancer cases after median follow-up of 20.1 years.

effect_size.excerpt: Dietary zinc intake was positively associated with higher kidney cancer risk; the HR comparing the extreme quartiles of zinc intake was 1.74 (95% CI: 1.02-2.97; P-trend = 0.033).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Dietary zinc intake was positively associated with higher kidney cancer risk; the HR comparing the extreme quartiles of zinc intake was 1.74 (95% CI: 1.02-2.97; P-trend = 0.033).

comparison.excerpt: the HR comparing the extreme quartiles of zinc intake

design.excerpt: We used data from the prospective Singapore Chinese Health Study

timing.excerpt: We prospectively assessed the associations of dietary zinc and other trace elements with kidney cancer risk

exposure_measurement.excerpt: A validated food frequency questionnaire and the Singapore Food Composition Database was used to compute the values of intake for zinc, copper and manganese.

gender.excerpt: recruited 63,257 adult Chinese residing in Singapore
